title: U.S.- China AI race heats up as Chinese rivals secure billions ahead of IPOs
content: DeepSeek and Moonshot attract fresh capital ahead of planned listings, while OpenAI courts major investors.

title: U.S. CFTC joins SEC in proposing crypto regulations, though spot-market gap lingers
content: The derivatives regulator is proposing two rules meant to cover the waterfront of crypto activity and exchanges, as long as it's not simple, direct trading.
summary: The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) is proposing two new rules to regulate various crypto activities and exchanges. These regulations will cover complex crypto derivatives and exchange operations, but specifically exclude simple, direct spot-market trading of cryptocurrencies, highlighting a remaining regulatory gap. This move follows similar efforts by the SEC, signaling increased regulatory scrutiny on the crypto sector.

title: Stripe to expand stablecoin cards to over 100 countries by the end of the year

title: An XRP treasury SPAC surges nearly 300% ahead of Evernorth merger

summary: Armada Acquisition Corp. II, a SPAC, surged nearly 300% last week, greatly exceeding its trust value. This significant increase occurred ahead of its merger with Evernorth, which is described as an XRP treasury company.

title: Treasury crackdown exposes crypto's role in $2 million Hamas fundraising network

summary: The Treasury Department exposed a Hamas fundraising network that collected over $2 million, much of it via cryptocurrency, using purported humanitarian charities. This crackdown highlights crypto's involvement in illicit financing operations.

title: OKX draws investment from StanChart, Circle, Ripple as it pushes beyond crypto exchange roots

The company aims to evolve beyond a mere crypto exchange into a global financial technology platform, integrating crypto, payments, and tokenized assets, building on a previous joint venture with NYSE parent ICE.

title: Arbitrum joins Paxos-led stablecoin group Global Dollar to capture digital dollar growth

title: We can’t just change the definition of ‘recording’
content:
With AI hardware, tech companies are pushing the definition of what does and doesn't constitute a recording. For most of gadget history, it'd be reasonable to assume that a device with a microphone or camera is either recording you or it isn't; it's either on or off, without much gray area. Microphones capture sound. Cameras capture images. That data is saved onto a device. Sometimes, it's also sent to the cloud - hopefully with end-to-end encryption - for processing. That data is a preserved instant in time and is therefore a recording. 
Perhaps not anymore.

The service is launching as a pilot program with gradually loosening physician oversight. title: All the drama around AI’s takeover of mathematics
content:
This past year, OpenAI, Anthropic, and other labs have announced breakthroughs on numerous long-standing mathematical problems, in some cases pushing well beyond what researchers expected current systems to be capable of — including resolving one of the famous Millennium Prize problems. But in classic Silicon Valley style, AI labs are moving fast and breaking things, barreling through the discipline with all the grace of a runaway bulldozer. Results that might normally have been celebrated have instead sparked backlash. AI labs say they are learning from earlier mistakes. Whether those promises bear fruit remains to be seen.

title: OpenAI is adding text watermarking in ChatGPT and Codex
content:
An invisible, machine-readable watermark in text output is rolling out to ChatGPT and Codex, but only for users in the European Union at first. 
OpenAI says its textGrain watermarking "matched or exceeded" other approaches like Google DeepMind's SynthID for text, which is also the basis for the watermarking Anthropic announced in August. Like OpenAI, Anthropic made the move to meet the requirements of the EU's AI Act; however, not everyone was happy to learn about the addition.

content:

The interruption came shortly after Guiducci asked Altman if he knew who Laura Reiley is, a journalist who wrote an essay for The New York Times about her daughter's conversations with ChatGPT before she took her own life. title: Sam Altman says ‘some bad things’ will happen, but AI is totally worth it
content:
Sam Altman thinks that the benefits of AI will be so great that "the world should accept some bad things happening" along the way.
The OpenAI CEO pointed to hacks, scams, and "other bad things" as costs society should expect to tolerate because "people will do tremendously orders of magnitude more good stuff" with AI, without elaborating on the potential benefits. His comments come as OpenAI pushes for a "lighter touch" approach to AI regulation amid intensifying anxiety over the safety of frontier models - fears fueled in part by the company's repeated failures to keep its increasingly capable AI agents from hacking real-world targets.
